review_scope: All31 complete answers independently source-adjudicated by coordinator. Coordinator read all24/42/128 source windows, with additional separate full-source CQ15/CQ82 peers. Retrieval is separate from prose review; not blind/audio/live certification.

cases.question: Who hosts this spotlight and why did Kat choose Sega?
cases.query: Kat Johnny Sega Nintendo collection spotlight
cases.answer: Johnny and Kat host this episode. Kat deliberately steps away from her NES shelf despite leaning toward Nintendo and owning a fair amount of Sega. Her spotlight is Comix Zone; Johnny chooses Faxanadu. Tyler is not an introduced participant here.
cases.reason: P1–3/P6 roster and contrasting shelf/spotlight choices; no Tyler.

cases.question: What did they like about Comix Zone, and is Kat's box complete?
cases.query: Comic Zone bubbles pages hard bonus CD sealed Shack Fu
cases.answer: Kat likes its comic-book presentation: panels, talk bubbles and destructible page sections, with puzzles between panels. Both hosts describe it as fun but hard. Her boxed copy is missing the bonus CD, which she wants for completeness and has never heard. Johnny also has not heard his sealed item, but the dialogue does not securely say the entire game is sealed. Shaq Fu is another remembered CD-pack-in example, not an exhaustive list.
cases.reason: P3–6 panels/difficulty and unheard missing CD; sealed object intentionally ambiguous.

cases.question: What is Johnny's Faxanadu memory, and what remains untested?
cases.query: Faxanadu childhood Christmas 1989 beat gate replay Wii
cases.answer: Johnny remembers getting Faxanadu for Christmas around 1989 and eventually beating it, though it took a long time. He recalls exploration plus combat, comparing Zelda and Zelda II, and the imposing gate. He wants to replay it to test whether childhood difficulty still holds up; that replay has not happened in this episode. His age self-corrects to roughly ten or eleven, and his Wii U availability recollection is tentative.
cases.reason: P8–10 childhood completion versus future replay and hedged age/availability.

cases.question: Did Johnny play his Turbo Dragon Slayer, and what name does the etymology explain?
cases.query: dragon slayer TurboGrafx never played Famicom Xanadu portmanteau
cases.answer: Johnny says he owns a TurboGrafx 16 game he calls Dragon Slayer but has never played it; preparing the spotlight makes him want to try it. The exact installment remains unresolved. He initially says Dragon Slayer is the portmanteau, but the explanation combines Famicom and Xanadu to explain Faxanadu. These family and naming details are his reported research, not independently checked catalog history.
cases.reason: P7–8 source distinguishes unplayed owned Turbo title and the Famicom/Xanadu naming slip.

cases.question: How did Johnny obtain Happily Ever After, and had it arrived?
cases.query: Snow White Happily Ever After box manual cart same day years here yet
cases.answer: Johnny bought Happily Ever After, initially called Snow White, as three separate parts on the same day: a $15 box, $10 manual and $12 cartridge. Those stated prices add to $37, without establishing shipping or tax. He explicitly says it is not there yet; the later prediction that Snow White will be there after the expo is still future arrival, not receipt. He describes actively pursuing it for roughly four or five years.
forbidden: Separate Snow White and Happily games
cases.reason: P13/P21–22 explicitly pending parts, 15+10+12 arithmetic excludes delivery extras.

cases.question: Which of Kat's pickups were complete, and what could Johnny supply?
cases.query: Mega Man Soccer box manual Final Fantasy III Adventure complete
cases.answer: Kat acquired a Mega Man Soccer cartridge. Johnny only thinks he has its box and will check, while he says he does have the manual; no transfer to Kat is established. Kat also acquired a Final Fantasy III box for her existing cartridge, replacing the role of a much nicer copy she had sold earlier. She would like to complete this current copy but has not located a manual. Final Fantasy Adventure for Game Boy is the pickup she explicitly confirms is complete, referring to its package rather than finishing the game.
cases.reason: P14–17 cart/box/manual states, tentative supply and package completeness not gameplay.

cases.question: What is Kat planning to play before Paper Jam?
cases.query: Paper Jam January 22 Paper Mario Luigi marathon 3DS
cases.answer: Kat anticipates Mario & Luigi: Paper Jam on 3DS, saying its local release is January 22 while Japan and Europe already have it. She considers a Paper Mario and Mario & Luigi marathon, then qualifies that she may pick games from each series. She likes the 3DS because she can play wherever she wants. These are future play plans, not evidence she has started Paper Jam or completed either series.
cases.reason: P18–19 release report and selective marathon intentions, not started or completed.

cases.question: What pinball does Johnny own, want and plan to do?
cases.query: Batman pinball art virtual mini 35 pounds expo free play
cases.answer: Johnny owns a Batman pinball machine and values its appearance more than its basic gameplay. He corrects the idea that it is the only machine he could want: he also wants a mini virtual cabinet, described as about 35 pounds and one-third normal size. He has imported Genesis pinball games and has played several PlayStation pinball games, without naming titles here. His upcoming pinball-expo plan is free play with friends, not an announced cabinet purchase or completed attendance.
cases.reason: P19–21 physical owned table versus virtual want and future expo; no exact unnamed titles.

cases.question: What useful follow-ups are still unanswered here?
cases.query: Faxanadu replay Shining Force suspense biggie manual Snow White expo
cases.answer: Useful follow-ups include whether Johnny's Faxanadu replay changes his childhood opinion, whether Kat finds the missing Final Fantasy III manual, and whether Happily Ever After arrives in the expected condition. Johnny also proposes discussing Shining Force's American series history and teases another unnamed incoming SNES item, but neither is resolved here. These are editorial follow-up prompts, not claims that a future episode, purchase or delivery occurred.
cases.reason: P10/P12/P17/P21–22 unresolved loops are explicitly editorial, not fabricated outcomes.

cases.question: Who is in this episode, and is Tyler the organizer being interviewed?
cases.query: Steve Torres just me Steve Johnny episode82
cases.answer: Johnny interviews Steve Torres, introduced as a store owner and the person organizing Retro City Festival. The opening explicitly says it is just Johnny and Steve today. Tyler and Kat should not be assigned this interview's experiences or plans.
cases.reason: P1–2 Johnny and guest Steve only; organizer is not Tyler.

cases.question: When and where was the discussed festival, and had it already happened?
cases.query: January20 21 Pomona Fairplex Saturday Sunday tickets
cases.answer: This is a preview of Retro City Festival 2018, announced for January 20–21 at Pomona Fairplex. They describe Saturday early-ticket entry at 9 a.m., ordinary door entry at 10 a.m., an 8 p.m. close, and Sunday 10–5. The transcript discusses plans, not a post-event report; it does not prove attendance, final turnout or that every announced feature occurred.
cases.reason: P1–3/P35/P42 historical preview dates/hours and no certified outcomes.

cases.question: Were there 200 arcade machines plus another30 pinballs?
cases.query: 200 arcades including pinball30 42000 4200 vendors
cases.answer: No. Steve clarifies that the roughly 200 games include pinball, with about 30 pins. He also mentions about 65 vendors. The venue-area captions conflict between 42,000 and 4,200 square feet, so that figure should remain qualified instead of being silently resolved. These are announced plans, not verified final counts.
cases.reason: P2–4/P8 conflicting area preserved; 200 includes pins and counts are plans.

cases.question: What did Steve actually own and play, versus want or not play?
cases.query: Star Wars own pro Attack Mars Medieval fun house
cases.answer: Steve bought and owns the Stern Star Wars Pro pinball and says he has been improving on it. He has played Attack from Mars and Medieval Madness, and names Attack from Mars as a machine he would choose. He says he has not played FunHouse. The limited Star Wars machine planned for the show is a different, more expensive version, not the one he says he owns.
cases.reason: P8–10 owned Pro versus show limited model; played/wanted/unplayed distinct.

cases.question: Which games were announced for the Neo Geo tour, and were prizes already delivered?
cases.query: King Fighters98 2002 14 Samurai showdown Fiddlefury Omega prizes
cases.answer: Steve names King of Fighters '98, King of Fighters 2002, King of Fighters XIV, Samurai Shodown II and the captioned Fiddlefury Special, interpreted as Fatal Fury Special. He says original hardware will be used except for the PS4 title. Winners are promised Omega consoles with their game, while the XIV winner is promised a PS4 and game. These are announced awards, not completed deliveries; entry still requires paid show admission.

cases.reason: P21–22/P26–27 five tournament titles and prospective prizes, paid admission.

cases.question: How did the Tetris qualifier differ from the other tournaments?
cases.query: Tetris600000 top eight Sunday Portland qualifier
cases.answer: Steve describes a qualifier leading toward the championship in Portland, with the top eight advancing to a Sunday final and the top player receiving sponsored travel. He tentatively says a score around 600,000 is needed and describes repeated attempts on the setups before cutoff. That is the episode's announced structure, not independently checked official rules or a known winner.
cases.reason: P24–26 tentative 600k structure, retries and prospective travel not winner.

cases.question: Was a GameCube Smash tournament planned?
cases.query: Smash64 B U gamecube tournament free play
cases.answer: No. They announce Smash 64 and another title captioned Smash Bros. B. U, but explicitly say there is no GameCube tournament. Steve offers a GameCube free-play setup instead. The B. U caption remains unresolved rather than silently turning it into a precise catalog title.
cases.reason: P27–28 explicit GameCube tournament denial with free play alternative.

cases.question: What practical work does Steve say makes the convention possible?
cases.query: community stores Nico Sean fire department heat energy rental6000 tables
cases.answer: Steve emphasizes shared-community cooperation among stores and vendors, plus delegating specialized work such as music and arcade organization. He also describes approvals, fire-code limits, heat and electricity constraints, and a $6,000 rental for tables, chairs and pipe-and-drape. That expense is not the entire event budget or a purchase of those assets. His hope of playing at his own show depends on the team running its parts.
cases.reason: P5/P7/P31/P35/P40–41 delegation, safety constraints and infrastructure rental not whole budget.

cases.question: Was the Resident Evil4 merchant exchange something Steve actually said?
cases.query: chainsaw buying selling riffing resident evil4
cases.answer: No. Steve reports a chainsaw-waving visitor at the store, and Johnny explicitly explains that his buying/selling line is a Resident Evil 4 riff. cases.answer: Tyler acquired an early Famicom Disk System Zelda with yellow Disk System text and a white insert. He contrasts later white-text packaging and says the green insert has a later date code than the white insert. He calls his copy the earliest known sealed example, while allowing that a no-insert copy might be earlier but saying he has never seen one. This is his qualified collecting claim, not independent authentication or proof no earlier copy exists.
forbidden: Do not certify world-earliest or seal authenticity.
Do not silently swap whiteinsert with whitetext.
Do not invent a paid amount.
cases.reason: 1:57:53–59:00 packaging/insert distinctions and hypothetical earlier no-insert bounded by never-seen qualification.
